```python
def compress(grid):
    """The grid without its frontiers: every row and every column that is one color throughout."""
    rows = {i for i, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1}
    cols = {j for j in range(len(grid[0])) if len({row[j] for row in grid}) == 1}
    return [[v for j, v in enumerate(row) if j not in cols] for i, row in enumerate(grid) if i not in rows]

def upscale(grid, factor):
    """Each cell as a factor x factor block of its color."""
    return [[v for v in row for _ in range(factor)] for row in grid for _ in range(factor)]

def crop(grid, top, left, height, width):
    """The height x width subgrid whose top-left cell is (top, left)."""
    return [row[left:left + width] for row in grid[top:top + height]]

def trim(grid):
    """The grid without its outermost rows and columns."""
    return [row[1:-1] for row in grid[1:-1]]

def replace(grid, old, new):
    """The grid with every cell of color old recolored new."""
    return [[new if v == old else v for v in row] for row in grid]

def hperiod(grid):
    """The smallest p such that every row repeats itself every p cells: the grid's width if none is smaller."""
    w = len(grid[0])
    return next(p for p in range(1, w + 1) if all(row[j] == row[j - p] for row in grid for j in range(p, w)))

# one task's program: the one shape, cut out by dropping every one-color row and column, mirrored left to right
from lib import compress
def transform(grid):

# another's: every cell as a block whose side is the number of colors other than the background
from lib import upscale
def transform(grid):
    return upscale(grid, len({v for row in grid for v in row}) - 1)
```

    """Number of cells of each color in the grid."""
    from collections import Counter
    return Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)

def background(grid):
    """The least common color in the grid."""
    return counts(grid).most_common()[-1][0]

def constant_columns(grid, value=None):
    """Indices of columns that are one color throughout (optionally that exact value)."""
    return [j for j in range(len(grid[0]))
            if len({row[j] for row in grid}) == 1 and (value is None or grid[0][j] == value)]

def split_halves(grid, div):
    """The left and right halves of the grid around column div (divider excluded)."""
    return [row[:div] for row in grid], [row[div + 1:] for row in grid]

def overlay_compare(grid, same, diff):
    """Split the grid at its uniform non-background divider column; each output cell is
    same where the two halves are equal and diff where they differ."""
    bg = background(grid)
    d = [j for j in constant_columns(grid) if grid[0][j] != bg]
    # prefer the divider whose value is not the background; fall back to any constant column
    div = d[0] if d else constant_columns(grid)[0]
    L, R = split_halves(grid, div)
    return [[same if l == r else diff for l, r in zip(lrow, rrow)] for lrow, rrow in zip(L, R)]

def shared_color(grid, div):
    """The color both halves have in common besides the divider: the shared background
    if the halves' backgrounds match, otherwise the shared accent color."""
    L, R = split_halves(grid, div)
    lb = background(L); rb = background(R)
    if lb == rb:
        return lb
    common = {v for row in L for v in row} & {v for row in R for v in row}
    common.discard(grid[0][div])
    return sorted(common)[0] if common else lb
